Title: How to choose the right way to install GitHub CLI (gh) on Linux/BSD — official first, community where necessary, avoid Snap
Description: Recommend a clear decision rule: prefer the official, maintainer-supported packages (Debian APT, RPM repos, Homebrew, precompiled binaries) for updates and support; use community/unofficial packages only when your platform lacks an official channel; do not install gh as a Snap per upstream guidance.
Audience: Developers, sysadmins, and Linux/BSD users deciding how to install or upgrade gh
Rationale: The source explicitly distinguishes between maintainer-supported official packages and community/unofficial packages, and it contains an explicit warning discouraging Snap. Communicating a simple decision rule (official → community → discouraged) gives readers a practical takeaway they can apply immediately when installing gh. Gaps and uncertainty: the source does not present comparative metrics (e.g., update latency, package signing details across all channels, or platform-specific caveats beyond provided commands), so the recommendation is based on stated support level rather than measured differences.
Evidence: Explicit statements: “Debian packages are hosted… These packages are supported by the GitHub CLI maintainers”; “Community (Unofficial)… The GitHub CLI team does not maintain the following packages or repositories. We are unable to provide support…”; and the Snap warning: “The GitHub CLI team actively discourages use of the following methods of installation… our team suggests never installing gh as a snap.” Example command groups provided for official APT, RPM (DNF4/DNF5/yum/zypper), Homebrew, and precompiled binaries demonstrate the official channels offered.
